description: An entry loop visits an object's keys and values in insertion order
Deleting a property and assigning it again moves its entry to the end
An instance lists its id first, then its constructor fields and derived properties
code:
class Room(width, depth):
    this.width = width
    this.depth = depth
$Room.area = $Room.width * $Room.depth
lab = Room(3, 4)
fields = []
for field, value of lab: fields.push(field)
fields

description: Entries are snapshotted before the first body, so changes in the body do not change the loop
code:
bills = {rent: 900, food: 300}
paid = []
for bill, amount of bills:
    bills.food = 0
    bills.fee = 25
    paid.push(amount)
[paid, bills.food, bills.fee]

description: A rolled-back try puts a deleted property back where it stood
A suppose block sees its own edits while the record keeps its order afterwards
Nested savepoints each restore the entries their own work changed
code:
o = {a: 1, b: 2, c: 3}
try:
    delete o.a
    try:
        delete o.b
        o.b = 5
        throw "inner"
    catch error:
        pass
    o.a = 7
    seen = []
    for key, value of o: seen.push(key + value)
    throw seen.join(" ")
catch error:
    inner = error
after = []
for key, value of o: after.push(key + value)
[inner, after]

description: A rolled-back field deletion keeps an instance's id first and its fields in order
code:
class Point(x, y):
    this.x = x
    this.y = y
p = Point(1, 2)
try:
    delete p.x
    p.x = 5
    throw "undo"
catch error:
    pass
fields = []
for field, value of p: fields.push(field + "=" + value)
fields

description: A function returns the first key whose value passes a limit
A two-name loop over a value that is not an object raises a TypeError
code:
xs = [1, 2]
failure = ""
try:
    for key, value of xs: pass
catch error:
    failure = error
failure
